siop_planned.comment: Optional fallback source of Planned Start for spools not found in the Weekly Production Planning workbook - see merge.py -> apply_siop_fallback(). Filename is inconsistent; this pattern just requires SIOP, then Planned, then Spools to appear in that order.

rework.comment: QA/QC's Production Rework Data workbook - lives in paths.quality_upload_folder (data/upload/quality/), NOT paths.upload_folder, since it's synced separately from the DPR/Weekly/Line History/SIOP files. Optional PDQC override source - see reader.py -> read_rework() and merge.py -> apply_rework_pdqc_override(). Also the source for the Quality Assurance/Control dashboard - see src/quality/ and config/quality_settings.json.

material_handover.comment: Material Handover tracking workbook (one row per spool) - lives in paths.production_upload_folder (data/upload/production/), the folder previously reserved for future Production-only charts (see that folder's README.txt and src/departments.py). Optional, best-effort source for the Material Handover section of the Production dashboard - see reader.py -> read_material_handover() and src/production/material_handover.py. A missing file only skips that section; it never blocks the rest of the Production dashboard.

welder_performance.comment: Welder Performance Record workbook (one row per welder/job/process entry) - lives in paths.quality_upload_folder (data/upload/quality/), same folder as the Rework Data workbook, synced separately from Drive. Optional, best-effort source for the Welder Performance section of the Quality dashboard - see reader.py -> read_welder_performance() and src/quality/welder_performance.py. A missing file only skips that section; it never blocks the rest of the Quality dashboard. header_row is 3 (0-indexed) because the sheet has a merged title row plus two blank rows before its real header.

project_master.comment: Project Code -> Project Name master list (2026-08-17), hand-maintained by the person and updated from time to time - lives in paths.upload_folder (data/upload/projects/), same folder as the DPR/Weekly/Line History workbooks. Optional - see reader.py -> read_project_master() and src/quality/reader.py, which merges it on top of the DPR-derived Project Code -> Name lookup (this file wins on any conflict, since it's the one he directly maintains) for the Quality dashboard's rework-by-project and Welder Performance project charts. A missing file just falls back to the DPR-derived lookup alone, same as before this file existed. Multiple Project Codes can share the same Project Name (e.g. several PO line items under one named project) - this is normal, not a data error.

inspection_data.comment: QC's continuous PDQC Inspection Data log (2026-09-02) - one row per offer-for-inspection event, first-time status only (Accept, or the specific rework/defect-type reason as free text), going back to 2023. Lives in paths.quality_upload_folder (data/upload/quality/), same folder as the Rework Data workbook. Filename varies but always starts with 'INSPECTION DATA'. Unlike every other source, this workbook has ~150 sheets: one per weekly window plus a couple of hand-built summary/tally sheets mixed in at arbitrary positions (not just the first sheet - see reader.py -> read_inspection_data()). Every sheet is scanned and any sheet whose columns match the expected shape is treated as data and combined; summary/tally sheets are skipped automatically because they don't have those columns, regardless of their name or position. Now the sole source for the Quality dashboard's Overview KPIs + 4 charts (kpis, first_offer_split, rework_by_project, rework_trend, rework_cycles in src/quality/summary.py) - replaces the Rework Data workbook for those specifically, per the person's explicit instruction. The Rework Data workbook is untouched everywhere else (PDQC/RFP Absolute Rules, top_rework_types, the Rework Data export/Welder Performance sections).

publishing.comment: When true, every pipeline run also copies the dashboard bundle (see output_files.dashboard_bundle above) into paths.website_data_folder (website/data/ by default) - that's the file the hosted website auto-loads for every viewer. Set to false if you only want the local upload-a-file workflow and don't want the published copy touched.
